target.quote: All evaluation evidence is pinned to that merge-base (plus the recorded overlay); nothing was re-tested against the newer upstream commits.

entries.corrected_statement: The quoted sentence is too broad and is withdrawn. It conflates two things and omits the pre-rebase evidence. Per the ticket-09 section 3 classification (class H = measured at the current tree, class P = pre-rebase), the evidence splits as follows. (1) AT-HEAD evidence (class H, ticket-09 lines 54, 55, 56, 57): the Bun candidate is the tree of `b6caf8c8`. `HEAD` differs from `b6caf8c8` only in the two evaluation workflows, the ci-refresh-01 report/evidence and (after `0bbb6e0f`) the ticket-09 report/evidence; the product, test and script tree is the same (computed from the receipts below). The Node control is `9af042ec` plus the recorded runtime-neutral overlay (the macOS rebase-01-test-04 overlay manifest lists 7 entries), NOT the candidate. That covers: macOS rebase-01-test-04 (RB4, candidate `b6caf8c8`, control `9af042ec` + overlay); ci-refresh-01 Linux `eval-bun-ci-07-11` and Windows `eval-bun-ci-08-09`/`08-10` (CIR; each tag commit differs from `b6caf8c8` only in the two workflow files); the dockquit helper (DQ, commit `a23e21b4`, an ancestor of `b6caf8c8`); and the bun.lock refresh (RBL, valid against the `8027cd8a` manifest; the fork-sync merge touched neither `package.json` nor `pnpm-lock.yaml`). The parenthetical "(the commit all evidence is pinned to)" that follows the merge-base in the same errata-01 paragraph is withdrawn for the same reason. The correct statement: at-head evidence is pinned to the candidate tree `b6caf8c8` measured against a `9af042ec`+overlay Node control; the merge-base of HEAD and `upstream/main` happens to be `9af042ec`, the same commit as the Node-control base. The rest of E-05e (the `upstream/main` observation and the ahead/behind counts) stands. (2) HISTORICAL pre-rebase evidence (class P, ticket-09 lines 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53) was measured on earlier frozen inputs. Apart from the T01 baseline (`f4e9fd50`, an ancestor of both HEAD and the backup branch, history only), those inputs are not in HEAD's history: `e5578080`, `7ce08fec`, `5a6b78ce`, `e94c0548`, `2c2707a3`, `58508e2b`, `b5ea6b65`, `8c674ca6` are ancestors of the local `backup/issue-2-pre-rebase-01` and not of HEAD (computed). That is the macOS build/startup (`5a6b78ce`), suite/lifecycle (`e94c0548`, `2c2707a3`), consumers (`2c2707a3`) and performance (`58508e2b`) evidence, the ticket-02 guard/install/security evidence (`e5578080`, `7ce08fec`), checkpoint B (`b5ea6b65`), and the ticket-07/08 pre-refresh runs (`8c674ca6` and the Windows 08-08 attempt, the latter's commit id not checked here). Ticket 09 already uses them only under its stated rule: pre-rebase evidence counts only where the rebase did not change the measured input, never alone for an adoption-critical claim whose input changed. (3) Upstream position, unchanged from errata-01: at 2026-10-14T14:10:06Z the unrefreshed local `upstream/main` was `11178c3c`; HEAD was 19 commits ahead and 18 behind it. No at-head evidence was measured against those newer upstream commits, and the pre-rebase evidence was not measured against upstream `9af042ec` at all.
entries.limits: Class assignments are ticket 09's own (section 3 table) and are cited, not re-judged. The Windows ticket-08 pre-refresh attempt (08-08) commit id was not looked up. `0bbb6e0f` is the ci-refresh-01 commit and `97c60acc` (HEAD) adds the ticket-09 documents. The ticket-09 sentence that HEAD `0bbb6e0f` differs from `b6caf8c8` in 4 paths is reproduced by the diff receipt; the diff to HEAD `97c60acc` adds the 2 ticket-09 files.

entries.origin: Sol phase 3 cleanup caution; corrects errata-01 E-06 C-12
entries.title: C-12: shared bytecode cache directory - `rm -r` withdrawn
entries.corrected_statement: The `rm -r ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python` suggestion in errata-01 C-12 is withdrawn: the directory is shared (errata-01 itself says its contents are not exclusively evaluation-owned) and must be left alone. File-level ownership can be shown for only 3 of its 71 files: the three D9 files `Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/glob.cpython-39.pyc`, `Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/fnmatch.cpython-39.pyc`, `Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/datetime.cpython-39.pyc` (D9 names them and the write time 2026-10-10T08:26:24Z; the receipt shows each exists with that exact mtime and no other file shares it). Only those 3 files are candidates for removal, and only by explicit user decision, with the caveat below; the other files are not attributed and are not candidates. If the user makes no such decision, leave the directory unchanged.
entries.limits: The other 68 files are not attributed to utm-dmg-verify-01 (mtime buckets by UTC date: {"2026-09-20": 16, "2026-10-08": 25, "2026-10-11": 27}). 16 of them are dated 2026-09-20, before the earliest evaluation date I looked at (2026-10-03, the ticket-02 acceptance record); the rest fall in the evaluation period and are likewise not attributed; one (`Users/slighter12/git/evaluations/Navide/issue-2-bun-toolchain/ticket-05-01/scripts/t05-run.cpython-39.pyc`) is a bytecode cache of an evaluation ticket-05 script path and is not covered by D9, and whether that one was disclosed elsewhere was not checked. None of the other files was attributed to any owner. Name plus exact mtime match is evidence, not proof, of sole authorship: the receipt does not show which process created each file, and the same system Python may legitimately recreate them on a later run. Python 3.9 regenerates these caches on demand, so removal is low-risk, but that is not an authorization.

entries.corrected_statement: Both removal suggestions are withdrawn as written and are not approved. The SSH directory `ticket-03-macos-guest-v1/ssh/` is part of the frozen ticket-03 evidence tree, and the raw evaluation root is the sole audit record that the tracked reports cite by path and hash. Neither may be removed, chmod'ed, moved or archived-then-deleted until the user records an explicit PRESERVATION DECISION first: what to keep (for example the full root, or an archive with preserved hashes and the anchors), where, and for how long. Until that decision exists, the status of both items is `keep`. Removing the SSH key material is a separate question from removing the evidence (it was not read or hashed by this work), and also needs that decision.
